Maya: Heads-up — saw steady KV cache mem growth on prod-cpupool-9 over the last 6h when long-context chat sessions are active. not a single big leak, looks like slow page residency growth and fragmentation.:thinking_face:
Samir: Can you paste the flame/prof sample? which metric is creeping?
Maya: pprof heap + our kv-residency counters. key lines:
```
kv.total_pages: 12432
kv.allocated_pages: 17340
kv.evictions: 1200 (low)
kv.page_fragmentation_ratio: 0.34
kv.prefix_reuse_hits: 0.08
kv.per_session_prefix_hits: 0.61
kv.page_pinned_seconds: 1.2e6
```
Maya: evictions are lower than expected given allocated pages, pages seem pinned by repeated small-key variants. attaching reproducer snippet: `PYTHONPATH=./tools python perf/repro/kv_longctx_reuse.py --clients 40 --ctx 12k`
Lia: That looks like repeated tiny prefix variants preventing compaction. Could be our fingerprint canonicalization: we truncate client-supplied prefix fingerprint to 64 bits and bake session-id fallback which makes many near-duplicates that differ by the last bytes => fragments across pages.
PerfBot: ALERT kv_mem_growth_prod-cpupool-9: 6h sustained increase, p95 mem +23%, p99 mem +31%. Suggested run: kv/compactness-check v2
Omar: Quick mitigation we can flip: enable per-tenant coalescing by canonicalizing trailing bytes (drop trailing 16 bits) OR increase eviction aggressiveness for low-hit prefixes. Which is less risky for correctness?
Samir: Dropping trailing bytes might hide real distinct prefixes (regression risk). Prefer eviction policy change first: treat pages with many low-hit prefixes as reclamation-first. Also add a short-session TTL for prefix entries created by fallback flow.
Maya: Ran a short A/B on a staging slice: switched to eviction-first for low-hit prefixes + session-ttl=45s. After 30m: allocated_pages down 9%, eviction rate up x2, fragmentation_ratio down to 0.21, end-to-end p50 latency unaffected. Small sample log: `kv.allocated_pages: 15880 -> 14470`
Lia: Good. We should also add deterministic instrumentation to track "prefix family" entropy (how many distinct trailing-byte variants per canonical prefix) so we can quantify collision vs fragmentation.
Samir: Agree. Action items: 1) roll eviction-first + short session ttl to canary for 24h (owner: Maya). 2) add prefix-family entropy metric and dashboard (owner: Lia). 3) add an opt-in safe canonicalization experiment (drop trailing 16 bits) behind feature flag for perf test only (owner: Omar). 4) write a quick postmortem if mem growth recurs (owner: Samir).
Maya: I'll kick off the canary deploy in 10m and post results. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
Omar: If canary is stable let's schedule a small perf-run that compares compactness and quality (regression suite) before wider rollout.
Maya: noted — will include the regression prompts.
PerfBot: NOTE canary started by Maya at 2164510200, check kv/compactness-check in 1h.
